title: Functorial Cartan--Eilenberg page realization without acyclicity
statement: Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B,\mathcal C$ be Grothendieck abelian categories with derived categories, and let $F:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$, $G:\mathcal B\to\mathcal C$ be additive left exact functors [def-sp-left-exact-additive]. For the presentations $P$ of [def-sp-cartan-eilenberg-presentation], there exist a filtered page-two model $M$ [def-sp-filtered-page-two-model], a functor $E:\mathcal A\to E_2\mathrm{SpectralSequence}(\mathcal C)$, and filtrations $L_P$ on $\operatorname{Tot}G(P.I)$ equal degreewise to the second degree filtration [def-sp-double-complex-total]. There are isomorphisms $s_P:E(P.X)\cong M.S(\operatorname{Tot}G(P.I),L_P)$ commuting with every presentation comparison: the filtered comparison has underlying map $\operatorname{Tot}G(c.\alpha)$ and $E(c.f)s_Q=s_PM.S(t)$. The page-two isomorphisms $e_X^{p,q}:E_2^{p,q}(X)\cong R^pG(R^qF(X))$ are natural in $X$. There are isomorphisms $c_X$ of $E(X)$ with the truncation spectral sequence of $RG(RF(X))$, and first-page comparisons $k_X^{p,q}$ with $H^{p+q}(RG(\tau_{\ge q}\tau_{<q+1}RF(X)))$. The map $k$ is the component of $c$ followed by the canonical spectral-object first-page isomorphism; $e$ is $k$ followed by the canonical derived single-degree truncation isomorphism. No assumption that $F$ sends injectives to $G$-acyclics is imposed.

source.place: Tags 015J, 015K, 015N and 015X; CE computation, functoriality and filtered comparison

proof.text: Apply the functorial page-two construction to the spectral-object functor X ↦ GrothendieckSpectralObject(F,G,X), obtaining E, c and the natural page-two comparison k.

Use the filtered Cartan–Eilenberg/truncation comparison for E and c. It supplies the common filtered page model, the second filtrations L, the comparisons s, the filtration equation, and compatibility with every presentation comparison.

Compose k with the existing upstream natural isomorphism CategoryTheory.Functor.grothendieckSpectralObjectHIso (WeilConjectures/CategoryTheory/SpectralSequence/Grothendieck.lean) to define e. Compose its naturality equation with hc, reassociating composition, to prove naturality of e. The two displayed equations are definitional. This step does not apply the DAG lemma on well-definedness of derived functors.
